raw_content:
Here is a simple example of how you can write a Semgrep rule for this vulnerability in YAML format:

```yaml
---
id: vun-spring-security-samples-4e3bec90
title: "Incorrect Authorization"
description: "The application uses Spring Security without proper authentication and authorization checks."
severity: WARNING
languages:
  - java
metadata:
  tags:
    - spring-security
  version:
    start: <=1.5.7
pattern:
  taint-mode:
    - "org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean"
    - "org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration"
    - "org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.configuration.EnableWebSecurity"
    - "org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.UserDetailsService"
    - "org.springframework.security.provisioning.InMemoryUserDetailsManager"
  - "org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain"
  - "org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity"
  - "org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.User"
  - "org.springframework.security.core.userdetails.UserDetails"
```

This rule will match if any of the listed classes are used in a Bean definition, which is often the case when using Spring Security. The taint-mode field specifies that Semgrep should only flag these classes as potential security vulnerabilities if they are directly related to handling user authentication and authorization.
